title: National Book Trust: State under Article 12?

scenes.dialogue: It is registered as a society, and it earns money selling books. So can the National Book Trust still be the State under the Constitution of India?
scenes.chip: 1 · IS A BOOK TRUST THE STATE?

scenes.dialogue: If it is the State, it must respect fundamental rights. A Full Bench of the Delhi High Court said yes, in twenty twelve. Fourteen years later, did the Supreme Court agree?
scenes.shown: If it is the State, it must respect fundamental rights. A Full Bench of the Delhi High Court said yes, in 2012. 14 years later, did the Supreme Court agree?

scenes.dialogue: Hi, I'm Ravishankar from LawWorld. On the sixth of November, Honourable Justices Prashant Kumar Mishra and Augustine George Masih ruled on the appeal.
scenes.shown: Hi, I'm Ravishankar from LawWorld. On 6 November, Honourable Justices Prashant Kumar Mishra and Augustine George Masih ruled on the appeal.

scenes.dialogue: The Government created the Trust in nineteen fifty seven, to publish good books at moderate prices. It appoints the Chairman, who serves at its pleasure.
scenes.shown: The Government created the Trust in 1957, to publish good books at moderate prices. It appoints the Chairman, who serves at its pleasure.

scenes.dialogue: Three Ministries sit on its governing body and executive committee, and the C A G audits its accounts. The High Court found this control deep and pervasive.
scenes.shown: Three Ministries sit on its governing body and Executive Committee, and the CAG audits its accounts. The High Court found this control deep and pervasive.

scenes.dialogue: In the Supreme Court, the Trust said it is a registered society, not a statutory corporation, and that grants are only one source of its income.
But under Ajay Hasia, a society can be the State. Under Pradeep Kumar Biswas, Government control must be pervasive, not merely regulatory.

scenes.dialogue: Finally, what did the Supreme Court decide? The Government's control over the Trust is pervasive, so it is the State under Article Twelve. The High Court was right.
scenes.shown: Finally, what did the Supreme Court decide? The Government's control over the Trust is pervasive, so it is the State under Article 12. The High Court was right.

scenes.dialogue: Being a society, or earning part of its own income, cannot change that. But this ruling does not make every employee a civil servant. The Trust's appeal was dismissed.
